# fasttrop

Estimate the effect of a policy or other treatment in panel data with
the Triply Robust Panel (TROP) estimator. The model fits run in C, so
the results come fast.

New here? [TROP in plain
words](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/the-big-idea.md) What
the method does and why its authors made it.

Ready to try it? [Get
started](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/fasttrop.md) Install
the package and make your first estimate.

Want the evidence? [How we checked
fasttrop](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/validation.md)
Agreement with other packages, tests, and simulations.

## What fasttrop does

Some units get a treatment, for example a new law, and other units do
not. fasttrop estimates how the treatment changed an outcome of the
treated units. For each treated unit and period, it calculates the
outcome without the treatment from the untreated data. Three ideas
control this calculation:

- Units with a similar history get more weight.
- Periods near the treated period get more weight.
- A model finds patterns that all units share over time.

The data select how much each idea counts. fasttrop then averages the
effects of all treated cells. This average is the average treatment
effect on the treated (ATT). The standard error and the confidence
interval show how uncertain the estimate is.

**Fast** In our benchmarks with one thread and fixed tuning parameters,
fasttrop was 25 to 174 times faster than the Python packages. Times
depend on the computer.

**Checked** On four test panels, the local ATTs of fasttrop and
`diff-diff` differed by at most 4e-8. The gap to the authors’ package is
up to 2.5e-5, the same as the gap between the two Python packages.

**Three designs** The local method can calculate results for block,
staggered, and general designs. The triple robustness proof is only for
a block design.

## Know the limits

- The triple robustness result has a proof only for a block design.
- The bootstrap interval is reliable only with many treated units.
  fasttrop gives a warning message below five treated units.
- The global method works only for a block design.
- The package cannot use covariates.
- In our simulation with larger trends for the treated units, TROP
  reduced the bias, but some bias stayed.
- fasttrop follows arXiv version 3 of the paper. A line-by-line check
  against the journal version is not complete.

The article [What TROP can and cannot
do](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/limits.md) explains each
limit.

## Install the package

fasttrop is not on CRAN at this time. To install the package from
GitHub, do these steps:

1.  Make sure that you have a C compiler. On Windows, Rtools has the
    compiler.
2.  If you do not have the `remotes` package, install it.
3.  Run this R code:

``` r

remotes::install_github("farach/fasttrop")
```

## A first example

``` r

library(fasttrop)

# A practice panel: 8 of 40 units get the treatment in the last 5 periods.
panel <- trop_simulate(n_units = 40, n_periods = 20, n_treated = 8, n_post = 5,
                       seed = 1)

fit <- trop(panel, outcome = "y", treatment = "d", unit = "unit", time = "time",
            cv_cells = 200, n_boot = 200, seed = 1)
summary(fit)
```

The article [Get
started](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/articles/fasttrop.md)
explains each step and the output.

## Who made what

The TROP method is from Susan Athey, Guido Imbens, Zhaonan Qu, and
Davide Viviano (2026). fasttrop is an independent R package by Alex
Farach. The authors of the method did not write this package. If you use
fasttrop, cite the paper. The [citation
page](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/authors.html#citation) gives the
references.

# Package index

## Estimate effects

Calculate the TROP estimate for a data frame or for matrices.

- [`trop()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop.md) :
  Triply Robust Panel (TROP) estimator
- [`trop_matrix()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_matrix.md)
  : TROP estimator for outcome and treatment matrices

## Read the results

Show a fit and get its parts.

- [`print(`*`<trop>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop-methods.md)
  [`summary(`*`<trop>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop-methods.md)
  [`print(`*`<summary.trop>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop-methods.md)
  [`coef(`*`<trop>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop-methods.md)
  [`confint(`*`<trop>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop-methods.md)
  [`vcov(`*`<trop>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop-methods.md)
  [`as.data.frame(`*`<trop>`*`)`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop-methods.md)
  :

  Methods for `trop` objects

## Settings

Set the solver options, the tuning grids, and the number of threads.

- [`trop_control()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_control.md)
  : Solver options
- [`trop_grid()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_grid.md)
  : Tuning grids
- [`trop_threads()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_threads.md)
  : Default number of threads

## Practice data

Make a panel with a known effect.

- [`trop_simulate()`](https://farach.github.io/fasttrop/reference/trop_simulate.md)
  : Simulated panel with a factor structure
